decision: DIFFERS -> W1 + W6 (two clauses of ONE sentence). clemson_hgic_1149 states "Dwarf cultivars should be planted or thinned 8 to 9 inches apart, whereas taller 2- to 3-foot zinnia cultivars should be spaced a foot apart." -> in_row [8,12] (dwarf 8-9, tall 12). Today's [9,12] has no page for 9 as a low; UF/IFAS FP623 'spaced 8 to 12 inches apart' agrees. Row: the live page states 'When planting multiple rows of zinnias, space the rows a foot apart.' (the worklist's '12 to 18 inches' sentence is no longer on the page); 'a foot' is read through the promote's IDIOMS table (ruled 2026-10-01) -> row [12,12]. Four prose strings restating 9-12 are re-authored to 8-12. [RULED 2026-10-01 (Trevor, session 3 review): the composite [8,12] stands (Clemson's cultivar sentence: dwarf 8-9 in, tall a foot; two clauses of one page, W6). The same page's direct-sowing line 'When the seedlings are 3 inches tall and, depending on the cultivar, thin them 8 to 24 inches apart' is a THINNING range and is not authored; plant_habit is unauthored this arc, so the composite is the honest crop-level figure.]

edits.new: Space plants about 8 to 12 inches apart and water the soil, not the leaves.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (Clemson: dwarf 8-9, tall a foot)

edits.new: Thin or space to 8 to 12 in; water at the base to keep foliage dry.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (Clemson: dwarf 8-9, tall a foot)

edits.new: Once seedlings have a few real leaves, thin them so plants stand about 8 to 12 inches apart. Giving them room for air to move helps prevent the white powdery mildew zinnias often get.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (Clemson: dwarf 8-9, tall a foot)

edits.new: Thin or space seedlings to 8 to 12 in once they have a few true leaves; generous spacing for airflow is a primary cultural defense against powdery mildew later.
edits.reason: restates the moved in-row figure (Clemson: dwarf 8-9, tall a foot)
